statement: One paper cup is 6 cm tall. When cups are stacked inside each other, each extra cup makes the stack 1 cm taller. How tall is a stack of 4 cups?

choices.misconception: I counted the 1 cm for each of the 3 extra cups and forgot the height of the first cup.
I counted 1 cm for each of the 4 cups and forgot that the first cup is 6 cm tall.
I started with 6 cm and then added 1 cm for all 4 cups, but the first cup only gives its own 6 cm.
I stood the 4 cups on top of each other without fitting them inside, so 4 x 6 = 24.

hints: Draw one cup, then two cups stacked, then three. What changes each time?
The first cup gives the full height. Every cup after the first only adds a small rim on top. Count how many cups come after the first one.
The first cup is 6 cm tall. The other 3 cups each add 1 cm.

solutions.reliable: The bottom cup is 6 cm tall. Each of the other 3 cups adds 1 cm, so together they add 3 cm. The stack is 6 + 3 = 9 cm tall. The idea to keep: in a stack, the first object is different from the rest, so count it on its own.
solutions.elegant: Make a small table. 1 cup: 6 cm. 2 cups: 7 cm. 3 cups: 8 cm. 4 cups: 9 cm. The idea to keep: a table of small cases shows the pattern and catches the first-cup trap.

whyOnTest: Drawing the diagram: a sketch of the stack shows that only the first cup counts in full, while every extra cup adds just its rim.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
